clue.text: Daring regiment's boldness in America

explanation.surface: A daredevil army unit's swagger is admired across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS (Special Air Service) is the British special forces regiment, motto 'Who Dares Wins'; its possessive, SAS'S, is spelt like the American slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: SAS'S is the possessive of the Special Air Service; sass is American slang for cheeky impudence or nerve.

clue.text: Must function as new, then switch position

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as
a switch can be set to on, one of its two positions

explanation.surface: An instruction that something must work like new before being moved elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase for an essential condition, something that must be present.

clue.text: One's recalled enthusiasm gripping one having a go at jumbos

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the letters of One's are taken in reverse order

parts.note: one = I, plus 's gives I'S

indicators.note: gripping says the word for enthusiasm holds another piece within it

parts.note: zest is keen enthusiasm
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone remembers their own keenness for criticising very large aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumbos' suggests jets, but here it means large people; the definition describes a person who mocks others for their size.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prejudiced against fat people attacks the overweight, here jokingly called jumbos.

clue.text: Try circle with diameter y times two pi

indicators.note: times two asks for the assembled letters to be written out a second time

parts.note: to have a go is to try
a circle is the shape of letter O
D is the usual abbreviation for diameter in geometry

explanation.surface: A geometry exercise about a circle's diameter, a variable y and two pi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pi' looks like the mathematical constant, but it is the crossword abbreviation for pious; the mathematical vocabulary throughout is camouflage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pi is short for pious, and a smugly virtuous person is called sanctimonious by detractors.

clue.text: Destroy bats besetting live breeding ground

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding, so the anagram is placed around another piece
bats means crazy, so the letters of Destroy are scrambled

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A command to wipe out bats that are harassing living creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the flying animals being destroyed, but it is the anagram signal meaning crazy; 'besetting' places the word for live within the scrambled letters, before their final D.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabed area where shellfish are reared or naturally multiply.

clue.text: Put new coat on and buttoned

explanation.surface: Someone repainted and fastened a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a room up is to redecorate it with fresh paint; to do a coat up is to fasten it, so both senses are past tense.

clue.text: Misunderstanding leading to power outage?

explanation.surface: A failure to understand that causes the lights to go out.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase literally: a break in electricity production; the question mark flags this whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of understanding between young and old people; literally a break in electricity production at a plant.

clue.text: After surgery doctor is due ritual worship

parts.note: OP is short for operation, i.e. surgery

indicators.note: doctor as a verb means tamper with, so the letters of is due are rearranged

explanation.surface: Following an operation, the physician is owed something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun in the medical scene, but it is the verb meaning alter, rearranging IS DUE to USDEI.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for the work of God, the term for liturgical worship, the Divine Office.

clue.text: Principle of Chinese reign a young revolutionary embraces

indicators.note: revolutionary as turning round means the letters are read backwards
the run of clue words embraces the letters, which sit inside them

explanation.surface: A youthful rebel takes hold of the rule of a Chinese dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' finds GNAY within 'reign a young', and 'revolutionary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chinese philosophy the active, masculine force paired with yin.

clue.text: Controls on jet short just as rounding sharp bends

indicators.note: rounding means going around, so the shortened phrase surrounds the other piece
short means the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: 'no less' means just as, as in 'no less good'
Z-bends are sharp road bends, drawn on signs as the letter Z

explanation.surface: Pilot's controls for a jet aircraft taking tight turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the phrase meaning just as, and 'rounding' wraps it around the sharp bends; 'jet' is a fluid jet, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Spouts that direct the stream from a hose or jet engine regulate its flow.

clue.text: Running superbly, as record book shows

parts.note: like is a synonym of as, in comparisons
to clock is to record, as a time or speed
a book is a written work

explanation.surface: A record book reveals how smoothly something is going.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for smooth, regular operation without a hitch.

clue.text: Byron work put on by university in new year

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on

indicators.note: in means the university letter goes inside the month

parts.note: January, abbreviated JAN, starts the new year

explanation.surface: A Byron piece is staged at a college at the start of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Byron's long satirical poem about the legendary Spanish seducer.

clue.text: Irascible but intelligent peer met eccentric duke

parts.note: quick means bright, sharp-witted

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever lord encountered a strange duke who was short-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' reworks PEER MET into TEMPERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily roused to anger, as an irascible person is.

clue.text: A number depart in it on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
in means the word for depart is placed inside it

parts.note: to go is to depart
in music, time means rhythm or beat

explanation.surface: Someone told to leave promptly from a particular place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' looks like a quantity but means a song: this Gershwin standard. In a down entry 'on' puts IGOT above RHYTHM.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or musical piece, and this is a Gershwin standard.

clue.text: Keep one in a dry, cold room

indicators.note: keep in the sense of hold, so the other letters contain one

parts.note: TT is teetotal, i.e. dry, abstaining from alcohol
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Store something in an arid, chilly space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a castle tower but it is the containment signal, with 'in' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A room under the roof of a house, a loft.

clue.text: Bringing about ten big bananas — reach inside

indicators.note: inside means the word for reach is placed within the anagram
bananas means crazy, so the letters of ten big are scrambled

parts.note: to get somewhere is to reach it

explanation.surface: Getting hold of ten large bananas by stretching in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but is the anagram signal meaning crazy, and 'inside' places the word for reach within the scrambled letters, after their first two.
explanation.definitionFit: To beget is to cause or produce, an old word for fathering offspring.

clue.text: Rows in gallery that borders on the hygienic?

indicators.note: in means the rows go inside the gallery

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre
lines are rows

explanation.surface: Rows of seats in a theatre gallery near a hygiene display.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'cleanliness is next to godliness': THE GODS are the highest, cheapest seats in a British theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb puts piety next to cleanliness, so piety borders on the hygienic.

clue.text: Old rolling pins females dumped

indicators.note: pins means holds fast, so the other letters enclose the females

parts.note: rolling, as in rolling in it, means rich, loaded
F is female, so FF is females

explanation.surface: A baker's antique rolling pins are thrown away by women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling pins' looks like kitchen equipment, but 'rolling' means rich and 'pins' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To unload a burden or get rid of something is to dump it.

clue.text: Curl hair do too much

explanation.surface: Overdo the hairstyling with curls.
explanation.definitionFit: To frizz hair into tight curls; also to fry or cook food until scorched, overdoing it.

clue.text: Open up crypt, finally

parts.note: up as in time's up, means over or finished

indicators.note: finally signals the last letter of crypt

explanation.surface: An order to break open a burial vault at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open up' looks like one phrase, but 'Open' is the definition and 'up' gives OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done publicly, unconcealed, not secret.

clue.text: Male solicitor's admission to censor?

parts.note: Ed is a male name
a tout solicits custom, so a tout would admit I tout

explanation.surface: A man's confession to a lawyer about the censor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but it is one who solicits trade, a tout, whose admission is 'I tout'.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove material from a text or film is to censor it.

clue.text: Observing sound hotel management: understanding husband

indicators.note: sound means the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: running a hotel or inn is innkeeping
wit is understanding or intelligence

explanation.surface: Watching a well-run hotel and a husband who understands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it is the homophone signal: INNKEEPING heard as INKEEPING.
explanation.definitionFit: In keeping with means conforming to, observing rules or customs.

clue.text: She inspired all but closed after a time

indicators.note: after means the following piece comes behind the era

parts.note: an era is a period, a time
a door pulled to is almost closed

explanation.surface: A woman who motivated everyone except those who shut down eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but closed' means nearly shut, like a door that is pulled to. Erato is a Greek Muse, a source of inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muse, the goddess of lyric and love poetry, inspired poets.

clue.text: See boss, half cut, following one leggy bird

indicators.note: following means the cut word comes after one

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: half cut means half the word's letters are removed

parts.note: a see is a diocese, whose boss is a bishop

explanation.surface: Visit a slightly drunk manager next to a long-legged bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it halves BISHOP to BIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird with a curved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Weapon from exotic collection in black, with alternative name

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: in means the collection goes inside the other letters

parts.note: aka means also known as, giving an alternative name
a zoo is a collection of exotic animals

explanation.surface: A weapon taken from a strange set in black, under a second name.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable rocket launcher used against tanks.

clue.text: Heroic achievement to obtain fleece?

explanation.surface: Jason's great deed to win the Golden Fleece.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Jason's quest; the question mark flags fleece as the verb, to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a daring feat; to exploit someone is to take advantage of them, to fleece them.

clue.text: When touring, has to see UK restaurant

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: On a tour, someone must visit a British eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' rearranges HAS TO SEE UK.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant specialising in grilled beef.

clue.text: Child the result had this couple married much earlier

indicators.note: much earlier says that in the answer the letter for married stood far further forward

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A child would have been born had this pair wed long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: move the M of the answer much earlier, to the front, and the result is MITE, a child.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a romantic couple, a pair known to be together.
